commands.evidence: 145 test files passed; 1146 tests passed; duration 236.19s.
Next.js 16.3.0 optimized production build compiled and generated 6/6 static pages; /game is static and /api/simulation/turn is dynamic.

First canonical run: 23 tests passed in 10.3 minutes using 1 worker. Second unchanged canonical run: 23 tests passed in 10.1 minutes using 1 worker. Both include Prompt 11, Prompt 12, Prompt 13 integration, and both supported Prompt 13 viewports.

rootCause: The Prompt 12 Stop assertion depended on a fixed 250ms response delay, so the request could finish before the Stop control was observed.

Two parallel Chromium workers ran MapLibre/WebGL and full-viewport screenshot cases concurrently; the failing parallel run recorded V8 JavaScript OOM and the 1920x1080 integration test exhausted its 300-second budget.
changes: The first-turn and cancellation handlers now wait on test-owned Promise gates. Tests confirm route arrival, visible Stop UI, and requesting phase before releasing or cancelling, with finally cleanup for both gates and pending route handlers.
playwright.config.ts sets fullyParallel=false and workers=1, serializing the GPU-heavy canonical suite without skipping tests or increasing the timeout.

environmentNotes: A preliminary PowerShell invocation of npx tsc --noEmit exited 1 because the host execution policy blocked npx.ps1 before TypeScript started. The Windows executable npx.cmd then ran the canonical command and exited 0.
Vitest emitted its existing future configLoader native warning; Playwright emitted the existing NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR warning. Neither introduced a test failure.

productionBundle.evidence: Across .next/static/chunks and .next/server/app: 0 browser-storage matches, 0 E2E scenario markers, 0 world-state-store-v2-fixture markers, and 0 fake-diplomacy markers.

e2eBundle.evidence: The PAX_E2E_BUILD-only scenario marker exists in exactly one .next-e2e client chunk as intended; no browser-storage or fake-diplomacy marker exists.

e2eStability.evidence: The unchanged canonical npm run test:e2e command completed 23/23 twice consecutively with one worker; no skip/fixme, V8 OOM, or timeout occurred.

secretLeak.evidence: Post-verification inspection found actual environment values only in generated Turbopack cache files (1 production-cache file and 3 E2E-cache files). Exactly .next/cache and .next-e2e/cache were removed; the application bundles remain available. The final audit checked 3 complete environment assignments across 791 source/report/doc/log/application-bundle files and found 0 assignment leaks; the raw OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL values also matched 0 files. No value was printed.

browserStorage.evidence: 0 localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB matches in production source and production application output. Three E2E specs contain only assertions that storage remains empty.

fixtureIsolation.evidence: scenario-debug-bridge.ts is a production no-op; next.config.ts aliases it only when PAX_E2E_BUILD=1. Production has 0 scenario markers and .next-e2e has the intentional deterministic fixture.

EconomyViewPort backed by authoritative economy and one shared nullable population value.
RelationshipViewPort backed by revisioned ordered country-pair scores.
WarsViewPort plus separately versioned front and occupation geometry.
DiplomacyViewPort and a nullable DiplomacyChannelPort that renders server responses only.

tests: Canonical 23/23 Playwright tests passed twice consecutively using the repository's one-worker configuration.
All production/E2E bundle, secret, browser-storage, fixture, authoritative-empty-state, overlay, acknowledgement, Prompt 11, and Prompt 12 audits passed.
knownLimitations: The authoritative political, economy/population, relationship, war/front, diplomacy, and server-save providers are future backend/domain work by design.
The E2E artifact intentionally contains deterministic scenario tooling and must never be deployed as the production .next output.
Screens below 1280x720 continue to use the explicit unsupported-screen layer.
Generated Turbopack cache directories were removed after verification because they retained environment values; future local builds may recreate them and require the same pre-handoff purge.
